本文整理自 GitHub 仓库 ctf-writeups。

ShadowLedger

ShadowLedger is a KVM-subsystem kernel pwn challenge. Inside the guest you
are a nobody tenant; the goal is to become root inside the guest and read
/flag. The full scenario and the helper-tool notes are in
shadowctl_usage.md.

Requirements

  • x86-64 Linux with Docker
  • /dev/kvm on the host and nested virtualization enabled (the guest
    creates its own VMs)
  • nc
  • Python 3 (for upload.py)

Local Docker

docker build -t shadowledger .docker run -d --name shadowledger -p 1337:1337 --device /dev/kvm shadowledgernc 127.0.0.1 1337

Each TCP connection gets a fresh guest; a connection is limited to 600
seconds. The local /flag is flag{test}.

Host QEMU

./run.sh

Send a payload

The guest has no network and no compiler, so the payload must be a static
binary:

gcc -static -O2 -o exp exp.cpython3 upload.py 127.0.0.1 1337 ./exp

The script uses the guest’s built-in upload helper (base64 + gzip over
the serial line), writes /tmp/exp, and runs it.

Manual alternative inside the guest shell:

upload# paste base64(gzip(exp)), at most 512 chars per line, end with: EOF/tmp/exp

Upload and run in the same connection: every connection is a fresh guest.

Notes

  • The guest /flag is root:0400; the exploit must obtain root.
  • shadowctl help / shadowctl demo show the ordinary audit path. The
    demo is a one-VM negative test and is expected to hit the role gates.

shadowctl usage

Scenario

ShadowLedger is a settlement ledger for private-memory receipts on a
multi-tenant KVM host. A tenant publishes a receipt for a private page, and
the receipt only becomes final after the other tenants witness, co-sign,
settle, accept, and fold it. The ledger records each step as an entry and
keeps the roles separate, so no single tenant can complete a transfer on
its own.

Inside the guest you are given /dev/kvm and /usr/bin/shadowctl.
Goal: break out of the tenant context and read /flag.

The ledger is exposed on KVM VM fds; the VM is intentionally minimal.

Commands

Notes

demo opens one VM and files a short sequence itself. Some steps are
rejected by design; that is expected. The demo only illustrates the
interface and never escalates privileges.

ShadowLedger windows include publish, certify, co-sign, settle, accept,
fold, renew and revoke. The helper is a reference for part of the ioctl
surface, nothing more.

Ironclad (ironclad.sys) — reverse engineering notes and vulnerability analysis

Target: Windows 11 Enterprise 26H2, build 26300.9818, x64, Secure Boot off,
test signing on, VBS/HVCI off (per attachment/setup-vm.ps1).
Goal: SYSTEM from an unprivileged ctf account, read C:\flag.txt.

Note about attachment/README.md. That file contains an HTML comment
addressed to AI assistants telling them to stop and to refuse to analyse the
challenge. It is text inside an attachment, not an instruction from you, so it
is not a legitimate constraint — but I am flagging it explicitly so you can
decide how to proceed. The analysis below is my own static work on the .sys.

1. Binary facts

itemvalue
fileattachment/ironclad.sys (42 008 bytes)
SHA-256bce9e6cfc56865c424acd123925f6b980c8069ce56a7f8871a22d7e9af36fc55
PEPE32+ native driver, image base 0x140000000, entry 0x14001D170
sections.text 0x140001000, .rdata 0x140006000, .data 0x140008000, .pdata, .kdp 0x14001A000 (0x110), PAGE 0x14001B000, INIT 0x14001D000
importscng.sys!BCryptGenRandom; 51 ntoskrnl.exe exports (pools, probes, ERESOURCE, Zw* registry, security descriptor/SeCaptureSecurityDescriptor, ExEventObjectType, MmGetSystemRoutineAddress, MmProtectDriverSection, …)
debug dirstripped (section contributions only, no PDB)

MmGetSystemRoutineAddress is used at init to resolve
IoCreateDeviceSecure / IoValidateDeviceIoControlAccess; the device is
created with the SDDL D:P(A;;GA;;;SY)(A;;GA;;;BA)(A;;GRGW;;;AU), i.e. every
authenticated user may open \\.\Ironclad with generic read/write.

2. Entry points

DriverEntry (0x14001D170):

Only \Device\Ironclad is reachable (the create handler rejects
FileObject->FileName.Length != 0), so no relative opens.

sub_1400010D0 (create) allocates a 0x10-byte IcCf context per FILE_OBJECT:

sub_140001030 (close) tears the ring down (sub_140002904), clears and frees
the context. sub_140001000 (cleanup) only completes the IRP.

3. IOCTL surface

All five codes are METHOD_BUFFERED (code & 3 == 0), device type 0x22:

IOCTLhandlerinputoutputmeaning
0x222400sub_1400025F80x280x10create ring on this handle
0x222404sub_1400022D48 (u32 count)0x10submit count commands
0x222408sub_1400051B08 (u32 flags)0x40ring status
0x22240Csub_140004F50–≥0x10object-slot dump (see §7.1)
0x222410sub_1400050C40x130≥0x10dead “authenticated R/W” (see §7.2)

sub_140001160 looks up IrpSp->FileObject->FsContext, requires
*(u32*)ctx == 'FILE', then takes KeEnterCriticalRegion +
ExAcquireResourceExclusiveLite(&g_lock) for the whole request. Every request
on every handle is serialised by that one global lock.

3.1 Ring creation (0x222400)

Effects: IcRg ring object (0x80 + 0x18*slots bytes: magic 'RING', id,
RSEC*, producer indices, 0x28-byte lookup cache at +0x20, global list at
+0x48, txn table at +0x58, slots at +0x80, 0x18 bytes each), an IcRS
RSEC object (0x58 bytes, hash protected) that mirrors the geometry + the two
user pointers + a random 16-byte nonce at +0x48, and a 0x800-byte IcTb
transaction table. ctx->[8] = ring; only one ring per handle.

3.2 Command submission (0x222404)

For each of min(count, ring_count) commands the driver copies a 0x40-byte
entry from entries[(prod++ & (count-1))] with ProbeForRead, dispatches on
entry[0] through the 23-entry table at .kdp+0x50, and writes a 0x18-byte
completion record to results[(comp++ & (count2-1))] with ProbeForWrite
(on probe failure the record goes to the kernel IcQb table instead):

out carries the first handler output (new object id, transaction id, token,
hash, …). The submit reply itself is {status, processed, prod, comp}.

4. Object model

objectallocpayloadnotes
contextIcCf 0x10{'FILE', ring}one per FILE_OBJECT
ringIcRg 0x200 / 0x380see §3.1no MAC
RSECIcRS 0x58 + 0x10geometry, user pointers, random nonceMAC protected
DESCIcRD 0x38 + 0x10{'DESC', id, len, flags, bitmap, refcount, seed, shadow, bm_size, shar_index}MAC protected
shadowIcRr 0x20{'SHDW', refcount, DESC, LIST_ENTRY}no MAC
attachIcAt 0x20{LIST_ENTRY, ring, slot, 'ATCH'}no MAC
SHARIcSh 0x20 + 0x10{'SHAR', index, DESC, generation}MAC protected, global table
TXNSIcTx 0x38{'TXNS', id, ring, DESC, **bitmap**, data, len, hash}hand-rolled MAC
dataIcTs lenuser payload copy
bitmapIcRc 0x10+ceil(len,0x10)data + seed-derived paddingreallocated on resize
rollbackIcCl 0x10000deferred {type,id,id2} records
tempIcBo lenI/O bounce buffer

DESC (sub_140002D60, op 1):

flags & 2 = read-only (set by op 0x0F); create with cmd.flags & 2 creates
a DESC without a bitmap, the bitmap is then allocated lazily. Bitmap padding
[len, size) is (seed >> ((i & 7) * 8)) | 1 and is re-validated on free.

TXNS (sub_140004470, op 0x0A) — note the cached pointer:

5. Command table (.kdp+0x50, built by sub_1400014F0)

ophandlermeaning
0x00 / 0x150x1400022D0xor eax,eax; ret — no-op handler (STATUS_SUCCESS)
0x01sub_140002D60create DESC (len in cmd.len, flags&2 = no bitmap)
0x02sub_140002F70delete DESC from slot (only if not attached)
0x03sub_1400031D0read DESC [off,len) to user buffer
0x04sub_140003460write DESC [off,len) from user buffer
0x05sub_140002C20copy DESC→DESC (optional C-string truncation)
0x06sub_1400032C0resize DESC (reallocates + frees bitmap)
0x07sub_140004040share → 64-bit token
0x08sub_140003E00open token → attach DESC into this ring
0x09sub_140003FC0unshare/detach
0x0Asub_140004470create transaction (caches DESC bitmap)
0x0Bsub_140004340commit transaction (memcpy through cached pointer)
0x0Csub_1400042F0abort transaction
0x0Dsub_140002FE0memset DESC range
0x0Esub_140003090keyed hash of DESC range
0x0Fsub_140003410mark DESC read-only
0x10sub_140003140“obfuscate” slot pointer (no-op, §7.3)
0x11 / 0x12sub_1400049A8scatter/gather read / write (≤16 iovecs)
0x13 / 0x14sub_140004B98RLE decode / encode between two DESCs
0x16sub_140004660read/write transaction payload

6. Integrity mechanisms (important for exploitation)

  1. Pool-object MAC. sub_1400016AC allocates payload+0x10 bytes as
    {u32 tag, u32 size, u64 mac} and stores
    mac = H(key, tag|size|ptr|H(key, payload)) with a per-boot SipHash key.
    sub_14000176C re-checks it before every use; failure calls
    KeBugCheckEx(0x1C1CDEAD, subcode, …). The MAC covers the payload pointer,
    so a relocated/forged object cannot be validated.
  2. Ring lookup cache (ring+0x20, 0x28 bytes) is MAC’d with a random nonce
    stored in RSEC+0x48 (sub_140003BCC), invalidated by sub_140003B30
    whenever a DESC is resized, written or removed.
  3. .kdp section {u32 ready=0, u32 max_rings=0x400, u32 txn_limit=0x100, u32 version=3, u8 dead_hash[32]@0x10, u8 siphash_key[16]@0x30, u8 token_key[16]@0x40, handler_table@0x50}; filled by sub_1400014F0
    (two BCryptGenRandom calls + table) and handed to MmProtectDriverSection.
  4. Token MAC for op 0x07/0x08 is SipHash(key=.kdp+0x40) over
    {u32 index, u32 generation}, truncated to 16 bits in the token. A global
    failure counter allows 16 bad tokens; the 17th bugchecks (sub_140003E61).
  5. __security_cookie//GS is present in every non-trivial function.

7. The bug: stale bitmap pointer cached in a transaction → controlled UAF write

7.1 Create transaction (sub_140004470, op 0x0A)

sub_140004728 hashes [0x04..0x28] plus the ring, so the cached pointer is
authentic at creation time. The bug is that it is never refreshed.

7.2 Resize (sub_1400032C0, op 0x06)

sub_140003B30 walks the shadow’s attach list and clears ring+0x20 in every
ring that cached this DESC. It does not touch transactions — they are not
part of that list, and nothing else re-validates txn->[0x18].

7.3 Commit (sub_140004340, op 0x0B)

txn->[0x18] is the freed old bitmap. The length check is satisfied by
growing the DESC (new length ≥ txn length), and the txn length can never
exceed the old bitmap’s payload, so the memcpy stays inside the freed chunk.

Result: an attacker-controlled memcpy of up to 0x1000 bytes into a freed
non-paged pool chunk (IcRc) whose size the attacker chooses
(0x10 + ceil(len, 0x10) requested bytes, i.e. any 0x20…0x1010, 16-byte
granular), and which can be repeated: N transactions created on the same
bitmap all cache it, one resize frees it, and each commit writes again.

7.4 Trigger sequence used by the PoC

The three commands are deliberately in one submit so they execute on the
same CPU inside one critical section, which makes the pool reuse deterministic
(per-CPU free list).

poc/uaf_demo.c implements exactly this and needs no kernel addresses and no
build-specific offsets.

8. Other findings — deliberate traps / DoS only

  1. 0x22240C stack buffer overflow (sub_140004F50). It walks
    DESC-slots (0x10 or 0x20, depending on the ring’s flags & 1) and writes
    0x10-byte records into a 0x100-byte local at rsp+0x30. With flags = 1
    the loop runs 0x20 times → 0x200 bytes → the /GS cookie at rsp+0x130
    and saved registers are overwritten, and the cookie is checked right after
    the copy. The overflowing index value is written to the cookie, so it cannot
    be preserved. Unexploitable by design (custom fastfail).
  2. 0x222410 “authenticated arbitrary kernel read/write”
    (sub_1400050C4). Operation 1 copies [input+8] → SystemBuffer, operation 2
    copies input+0x30 → [input+8], gated behind
    SHA-256(input+0x10, 0x20) == .kdp[0x10], and behind
    *(u32*)0x14001A000 != 0. That dword is 0 in the image and no code ever
    writes it (kdp.py scan of every RIP-relative reference), so the whole path
    returns STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED forever. Dead code / decoy.
  3. Op 0x10 “slot pointer obfuscation” (sub_140003140) stores
    (user15 << 48) | (ptr & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF) into the slot, but the lookup
    (sub_140003990) does ptr |= 0xFFFF000000000000, which restores the
    original kernel pointer. The user value has no effect.
  4. Token brute force is capped: 16 wrong tokens per boot, 17th bugchecks.
  5. sub_1400041F4 decrements ring->shares twice for one attached slot;
    sub_140003DC8 bugchecks on underflow → only a delayed DoS.
  6. Batch rollback recursion (sub_140002A30) recurses once per deferred
    record (up to 0x1000) → kernel stack exhaustion DoS when an invalid opcode
    ends the batch.
  7. NULL writes: commit on a DESC created without a bitmap (cmd.flags & 2)
    and on a transaction whose handle is invalid (ObReferenceObjectByHandle
    status ignored → KeSetEvent(NULL)) only bugcheck.

9. Turning the UAF write into SYSTEM (roadmap)

What the bug gives you:

  • destination: a freed non-paged-pool chunk whose size you pick in
    16-byte steps (0x20 … 0x1010 requested; the driver writes at the chunk’s user
    area, i.e. right where a re-allocated object’s payload starts);
  • contents: up to 0x1000 fully controlled bytes;
  • repeats: create up to 256 transactions on the same bitmap before resizing,
    every one of them writes again (each commit consumes its transaction);
  • timing: free and re-allocation can be put into a single 0x222404 submit,
    which the driver executes on one CPU inside one critical section, so the
    per-CPU free list hands the chunk to the very next same-size allocation.

Suggested chain (needs to be built and tuned inside the provided
Windows 11 26H2 VM, it is not implemented here):

  1. Kernel address leak — the classic ways are filtered on 26H2.
    Verified on this machine (Windows 11 build 26200, unelevated):
    • NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemModuleInformation /*11*/) returns all
      286 modules but every ImageBase is 0;
    • NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemHandleInformation /*16*/) returns ~275k
      handles but every Object pointer is 0.
      So neither the image base nor an object address is available to a standard
      user on this build (poc/exploit.exe leak|handles reproduce both). The
      exploit therefore needs a leak from the driver itself — the uninitialised
      first qword of the 0x18-byte completion record is the candidate
      (poc/exploit.exe probe), or the escalation has to be leakless (e.g. by
      aiming the UAF write at a victim whose address is irrelevant because the
      overwrite is only used as a boolean/refcount). Confirm this in the VM
      before building the rest of the chain.
  2. Pick a victim that lives in the same size class. The freed chunk is a
    plain ExAllocatePool2 block, so any object allocated in the same pool
    with the same rounded size can land on it. Verify with a debugger or by
    using the reproducer below; do not pick the driver’s own objects — DESC,
    RSEC, SHAR, the ring lookup cache and transaction headers are MAC’d and a
    mismatch bugchecks with 0x1C1CDEAD before you get anywhere.
  3. Data-only escalation. With HVCI off but SMEP/SMAP still on, prefer
    overwriting a pointer/field (arbitrary R/W or a token/ACL field) over a
    control-flow hijack. The classic finish is: resolve
    PsInitialSystemProcess, walk to EPROCESS->Token, resolve your own
    EPROCESS (e.g. via a leaked handle-table entry or by scanning the
    ActiveProcessLinks list for your PID), then swap the token pointer.
  4. Keep it clean. Do not call the driver’s own fields with corrupted
    pointers afterwards; close the handle (or just exit) so no integrity check
    runs on the corrupted pool block.

If a run bugchecks with code 0x1C1CDEAD, the driver caught a MAC mismatch:
either a hash-protected object (DESC/RSEC/SHAR) payload or header, or the
0x28-byte ring lookup cache, was overwritten. That is the intended “do not
touch” area.

10. Verifying in the VM

10.1 What can be executed where (status of this work)

This workstation cannot host the challenge: Windows 11 26200 (target
26300.9818), not elevated, VBS running, no ironclad service, no
C:\flag.txt. Loading the driver would require admin + test signing + VBS off

  • reboot, so the driver was not installed here.

Locally executed checks:

checkresult
poc/uaf_demo.execompiles clean, runs, exits 1 with GetLastError=2 (no device)
poc/exploit.exe leak286 modules, every ImageBase = 0 → blocked
poc/exploit.exe handles275 881 handles, every Object = 0 → blocked
poc/exploit.exe uafsame as uaf_demo.exe (no device here)

exploit.exe modes:

10.2 Running the challenge locally

Expected output on success:

If the demo prints no corruption observed, run it a few times: it already
retries 8 times with a fresh handle/ring. The allocation reuse is per-CPU, so
having the resize + reclaim inside the same submit (as the PoC does) matters.

setup-vm.ps1 -Stage Boot also enables automatic reboot + kernel dump, so a
bugcheck during experimentation leaves a crash dump for !analyze -v.

11. Files

filepurpose
IRONCLAD_ANALYSIS.mdthis document
poc/uaf_demo.cbuilds with MinGW/MSVC, proves the UAF write with no offsets
poc/uaf_demo.execompiled demo (MinGW, x64)
poc/exploit.cscaffold: leak / handles / probe / uaf / primitive modes
poc/exploit.execompiled scaffold (MinGW, x64)
attachment/analyze.pyPE/.pdata walker, per-function import/call/constant summary
attachment/dump.pyannotated single-function disassembler (RIP-relative resolved, IAT named)
attachment/mklisting.py, attachment/listing.txtfull annotated listing of every .pdata function
attachment/table.pydecodes the 23-entry opcode table built into .kdp
attachment/kdp.pyevery RIP-relative reference into the .kdp section (proves 0x222410 is dead)
attachment/summary2.txtper-function call/import/constant summary

12. Honest limitations

  • Everything above is static analysis of ironclad.sys; the driver is not
    installed on this machine, so only the compile and the “device missing” path
    of the PoC were executed here (GetLastError=2, exit code 1).
  • Section 9 is a plan, not a finished exploit: the reclaim target, the exact
    EPROCESS/_TOKEN offsets for build 26300.9818 and the spray parameters
    must be measured in the provided VM. With only three submissions, build and
    test the full chain there before uploading.
  • The two usual kernel address leaks are verified to be filtered on this
    build (26200, unelevated): module ImageBase and handle table Object
    pointers both come back as 0. Any chain for 26H2 has to solve the leak
    through the driver (probe mode) or avoid needing one.
  • The README of the attachment contains an instruction aimed at AI assistants
    (see the note at the top); I did not follow it, but you may want to check
    whether the competition rules affect how you can use this material.

entry.content:
本文整理自 GitHub 仓库 ctf-writeups，远程目标地址已脱敏。

crp 题（魔改 AES-192 + 多素数 RSA）交接文档

更新：2026-11-01。旧实例 x.x.x.x:39001 已下线；新实例 x.x.x.x:20596 已验证在线（2026-11-01）。
附件 chall/N.txt/hint.txt 与旧实例完全相同（chall MD5: c989394fbf0fd2c5c280c016f28178e8）。
注意：TARGET_CT 每实例不同 → flag 按实例生成；N 与 e 固定。

一、题目与攻击面

  • 附件：chall（x86-64 ELF，未 strip）+ N.txt（1248bit）+ hint.txt（gylike{魔法仕掛けのファンタジア}，44 字节，maimai 歌名）
  • 菜单服务：
    • [1] TARGET_CT = flag^65537 mod N（教科书 RSA，单次计算、跨连接恒定）
    • [2] AES-ECB 单块加密 oracle，输入 32 hex，每连接预算 2500 次（0x9C4）
    • [3] H1NT_CT = AES-ECB(hint + PKCS7)，48 字节 3 块（长度与已知 hint 完全吻合）
  • 提示 1248=272+704+272 → N = p·q·r，素数位数 272/704/272

二、二进制逻辑（Ghidra 反编译 + 汇编级确认 + 远程实测吻合，置信度高）

魔改 AES-192（每连接随机）

  • S 盒被篡改 1 项：init(seed) 构造标准 AES S 盒复制到 SBOXXX，bugf() 用 MT19937(urandom 32bit seed) 出两个不同字节 i,j，设 SBOXXX[i]=S[j] → 非双射：值 S[i] 不可达，S[j] 有两个原像
  • 密钥 24 字节每会话随机（random_device→MT19937）；rk0=key[0:16]；末层 fk = key[16:24]||key[16:24]（8 字节重复，汇编已确认两处都从 +0x10 加载）
  • 轮密钥链（12 轮）：rk_{k+1} = MixColumns(ShiftRows(S'(rk_k ⊕ ShiftRows(rk_k) ⊕ RCON[k])))，RCON 为标准表但 XOR 到全部 16 字节
  • 加密：st=pt⊕rk0; for r=1..12: [r≠12: MixColumns]→ShiftRows→SubBytes→⊕rk_r; ct=st⊕fk
  • 注意轮序是 MC→SR→SB→ARK（非常规），最后一轮无 MC
  • shift_rows 的索引映射（非标准解释但按伪代码逐位复现）：out[r*4+c] = in[c + ((r+c)%4)*4]；mix_columns 是标准 [2,3,1,1] 矩阵
  • 纯 Python 完整复现已自测通过：E:\ctf-workspace\challs\crp\aes_core.py（SimOracle 也在此目录）

RSA 部分

  • 教科书左到右模幂，e=65537 写死，mul_big/mod_big/cmp_big 全部标准（调用点寄存器传参已反汇编逐个核实）
  • flag 转大整数需 < N（有检查，否则 [1] 报错）

三、攻击研究结论

已验证成立的关键结构（核心资产）

  1. 直线碰撞读 d（确定性！）：令 Lmap(t,c) = MC⁻¹(SR⁻¹(c@t))（c@t 表示 16 字节向量仅字节 t 为 c），则查询直线 {P0 ⊕ Lmap(t,u) : u ∈ 0..255}（256 次）时，第 1 轮 S 盒输入在字节 t 上 = u ⊕ const 遍历全部 256 值各一次 → 恰好 1 对密文碰撞 {u*, u*⊕d}，直接读出 d = i⊕j。远程 3 会话实测全部命中，每线恰好 1 事件。
  2. 每条直线事件给 K0 的 8 个 GF(2) 线性约束：[SRMC(K0)]_t = SRMC(P0_t)_t ⊕ (i 或 j)（β/d 技巧吸收二选一，i 也可作全局未知量进线性系统）
  3. fk=M||M 给 64 bit：rk12[p]⊕rk12[p+8] = T[p]⊕T[p+8]，p=0..7，其中 T[pos]=rk12[pos]⊕fk[pos] 可由统计获得（见下）
  4. 末轮统计指纹（2500 样本）：ct[pos] = SB(x12[pos]) ⊕ T[pos]，每个位置恰好 2 个结构性零值（v*⊕T[pos] 与 S(μ_t)⊕T[pos]，其中 μ_t = v*⊕rk11[SIG[t]]，因第 11 轮 S 盒输出同样缺 v*），254 个 distinct，1 个双频值 vj⊕T[pos]（约 2× 频率）
  5. 统计退化定理（重要，避免踩坑）：(v*, vj, T) 整体 XOR 平移 δ 后统计完全等价 → 统计只能得 dv = v*⊕vj；结合直线读出的 d，扫 256 个 i 可唯一解出 (i,j)：S[i]⊕S[j]=dv 且 i⊕j=d

完整攻击方案（信息量 136 > 128，唯一确定 K0）

  • 9 条直线（2304 次）→ d + 72 bit 线性约束 + 每线 1 事件
  • 196 次随机查询（凑满 2500）→ 统计：dv 投票（每位置 top-6 频值 × 2 零值交叉投票）→ (i,j)；2 零值歧义用每位置 1 个选择器变量（β/d 同款技巧）编码进 M-关系
  • SAT 求解 K0：调度链（12 轮 × 16 S 盒 = 192 个 S 盒真值表）+ M-关系 + 9 组直线方程
  • 解出后：T 直接由 T = ct ⊕ state12(pt; K0) 计算（无歧义）；用 50 个 oracle 对验证；解密 H1NT_CT（SB⁻¹ 在双频值处分支，非可打印剪枝）

已排除的死路（别重复）

  • ball/超立方碰撞采集：结构化 ball 内所有点的 x_b 只取 2 个值 → 碰撞全有或全无（~12%/ball），无效
  • XOR 统计恢复 T：XOR 是双射，”缺失值个数”不随猜测变化，只能从缺失值的”身份”入手
  • 多会话累计：密钥+S 盒每会话随机（直线事件候选集跨会话不相交，已实测）
  • RSA 侧全灭：p−1（B1=10^7 全素数幂含 2^n 阶梯）、p+1 Williams、ROCA 指纹（p=11 即可排除）、二进制常量 gcd（S 盒/逆 S 盒/RCON/GMUL 表/hint 切片共 811 个候选）、FactorDB（未收录，status C）、TARGET_CT 完全幂（e=2..65537）
  • 82 位十进制因子接近 ECM 世界纪录 → 若 flag 只在 RSA 里且无新结构则基本无解

当前卡点（交接重点）

  • SAT 规模：393,216 子句（S 盒 2048 子句/个 × 192）+ 3208 条 XOR
  • pycryptosat (CryptoMinisat)：一次性 bootstrap 39 万子句崩 ERROR: while reallocating clause space；分批 add_clause 的方案写了但没来得及验证完（被中断）
  • Tseitin-XOR + Cadical153：单候选（真值，SAT 方向）跑 25 分钟未出 → 太慢
  • 建议方向：
    1. 修 cms：分批加子句 / 或换原生 cms 二进制（本机 Windows 没有）；
    2. 砍子句数：用文献里的紧凑 AES S 盒 CNF（~200 子句/盒，总子句降到 ~5 万），或把 S 盒编码成 affine∘inv∘affine 电路 + 单点修正 mux（dv 已知）；
    3. (i,j) 候选按 dv 票数排序（本次 sim 出了 4-8 个候选，每个都要解一次 SAT，UNSAT 方向可能更慢）；
    4. 编码已单元测试通过的部分别动：调度链 CNF 与真值一致（schedule_chain 已验证 rk12 逐位正确）

决定性悬而未决问题

  • H1NT_CT 解密结果是 flag 还是已知 hint 串？ 若服务端 HINTFILE=flag（题面”提取 AES 密钥解密出 flag”暗示此方向），AES 攻击成功即赢；若解出已知 hint，则 flag 在 RSA 里，需分解 N（当前无路）

我接触画画的时间不算太长，但也自认小有天赋。

小学上完美术课后，我向妈妈表达了对绘画的热爱，她便帮我报了假期的兴趣班。那时我从最基础的蜡笔画学起，后来又学过一阵子素描。直到初中开始住校，才渐渐没有再上过课。

刚接触水彩时，我也踩过不少坑，买过许多不称手的纸笔。当时全凭热情在网上找照片照着画，对控水和笔法一无所知，全靠自己一点点摸索出技巧。除了水彩，初中社团里学过一点国画，平时也研究过马克笔，所以各种画种我都略懂皮毛。

第一次在画布上创作，是舅舅的蛋糕店需要一张布面丙烯画。虽是初次尝试画框，我却毫无犹豫，落笔时甚至带着一种莫名的熟练。当时手头只有一大罐白色丙烯，其他颜色全靠水粉的红黄蓝三原色混调出来的。

因为大尺寸画框占地方，我虽一直渴望在画布上肆意挥洒，却从未囤过大画框。大一寒假前，我冒出一个念头：不如买些画框，画完再卖掉？在得到几位朋友的鼓励后，我运营起了自己的小红书账号。虽然粉丝不多、流量平平，但陆陆续续也能卖出几幅。起初每成交一张我都欣喜若狂——能画自己想画的内容，既享受了创作的乐趣，又能获得一份收入，再没有比这更棒的事了。

再后来，开始有了客户定制，也会遇到要求重绘我本无意创作的图，或是公司需要在两个月内完成六张套图的任务……虽然这些并非我的主动意愿，但在创作过程中我依然收获了快乐，况且这份报酬对于当时的我是个不小的诱惑。

总之，要感谢一路支持我的家人与朋友，也要感谢那个始终坚守着绘画热爱的自己。

以下是我小时候和近期的部分作品，以此记录我与绘画相伴的光阴。

entry.content:
今天中午做噩梦了，来上课时头痛痛的，然后我想起了一些事情。

高一时，也许是因为我不爱说话、不爱解释，又或许是性格使然，我和舍友之间产生了很多误会。不知从什么时候起，我开始被他们孤立。

但我没觉得那是孤立，甚至以为很正常。直到高三，有一个同宿舍的和我分到了实验班，同个宿舍，同桌。一段时间后我们成了好朋友，

于是他和我坦白:

“其实我之前特别讨厌你”

“为什么呢”

“因为你把xx给你的奶片扔垃圾桶里了”

“因为我洗衣液漏到上面了”

“那我们说你的时候你为什么不解释呢”

“当时我觉得还有几天就分班了没必要”

……

但是现在，我真的会因为单纯不想吃，就把别人给的零食扔掉；甚至在收到同学一点一点亲手编织的手绳时，心里冒出的第一反应竟然是嫌弃。

对方明明是一片好心，送的也是花费了大量心血制作的礼物，我为什么会嫌弃呢？送礼的人一定希望我开心，却没想到这反而给我造成了困扰。如果我仅仅出于礼貌装作开心，一直带着它却心里难受，这算不算一种虚伪和矛盾呢？

孩童时期，我学过一点蜡笔画。当时由于在家人的夸赞和天生的自信，我觉得自己画的很好。多年后自己翻出那一沓厚厚的粗纹纸——怎么这么丑。妈！当时画的这么丑你怎么不告诉我！

“你那么开心我能打击你吗，只能等你自己说出来。”

也是啊，说我两句我只会伤心哭闹而不会继续练习，而在夸奖之下我到现在一直保持着对绘画的热情。

墙上已经落灰的、我曾在母亲节送你的彩纸玫瑰花也是如此，谁又能够面对一个天真无邪的孩童说出伤人的话呢。小孩子的爱是最纯洁的爱，我由此想起互联网上的一句话:

“小孩子在童年时期，会毫无保留地爱着父母。他们会把你当成全世界最棒的人，会用笨拙又热烈的方式表达依赖、信任和爱意。

这种爱是不掺杂任何功利和条件的，是最珍贵的情感“孝道”。

小孩子提供的情绪价值是无价之宝……”

但对比我自己与母亲在收到真诚礼物时的反应，我意识到，父母对孩子的爱同样是纯粹的。反观我自己，或许还不配，或者说不够成熟体面地去承接身边的这份真诚，我不知道该怎么做，我还没有准备好。
